title: GeoJSON Validator: Syntax and Structure Check
description: Validate GeoJSON against RFC 7946 structure with the GeoJSON Validator — syntax errors and container mistakes caught in your browser. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a Feature whose 'coordinates' sit directly under the feature instead of inside a 'geometry' object is the classic structural slip this validator names in one paste.
quick_answer: The GeoJSON Validator checks pasted GeoJSON for JSON syntax errors and basic RFC 7946 container mistakes — wrong nesting, missing type fields, malformed positions. Paste a FeatureCollection, Feature or bare geometry and read a verdict that separates 'not JSON at all' from 'JSON, but not GeoJSON', entirely in your browser.

Deliberately breaking a valid file — remove a bracket, rename a key — and reading the verdict is the fastest GeoJSON course there is.

A missing closing brace is a syntax error: the text is not JSON. A FeatureCollection whose members lack 'type': 'Feature' parses fine as JSON but fails as GeoJSON. The validator reports which world your file broke in.

A position needs at least two numbers, longitude first: [−73.9719, 40.7681]. A one-number 'position' or a string in the array is a structural failure the checker catches before a renderer misplaces your data by an ocean.

popular_table.note: RFC 7946 (2016) is the whole specification — GeoJSON has no versions in the wild worth fearing, and no CRS field: coordinates are WGS84 longitude/latitude by definition.

faq: Does it check the right-hand rule for polygon rings?

RFC 7946 recommends exterior rings wind counterclockwise and holes clockwise. Many parsers ignore winding; the validator concentrates on syntax and container structure, and treats winding as the recommendation it is rather than a hard failure.
Lat/lon order — can it detect swaps?

A latitude beyond ±90 inside a position is detectable and flagged. A swapped pair that stays in range (both numbers plausible) cannot be convicted by structure alone — plot the file in the viewer; geography is the witness.
What about foreign members and extensions?
Extra members are legal in GeoJSON — the spec permits foreign members. The validator does not punish a file for carrying them.
Properties must be a JSON object or null on a Feature. An array or a bare string there is a structural error the checker names.
Can a single geometry (no Feature) validate?
Yes — bare geometry objects are complete GeoJSON. The validator accepts FeatureCollections, Features and geometries alike.
A geometry with empty coordinates is structurally tolerated by the spec's grammar but renders nothing — the validator flags emptiness as a warning worth reading.
